title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page states the Proposition announced at the bottom of the previous page. It is the basic 'surgery' dictionary for conformal surfaces.

(a) The first category consists of compact conformal (Riemann) surfaces X with boundary, together with:
- a chosen boundary component C, assumed real-analytic ('rectifiable', apparently in the sense of locally straightenable by an analytic chart rather than finite length);
- a 'torsorial structure' on C, i.e. a structure of torsor under the circle group SO(2) = O(2)/±1, compatible with the real-analytic structure.
Concretely this is an analytic identification of C with S^1, defined up to rotation.

(b) The second category consists of conformal surfaces X' with a pointed closed disc (D, a), where D ⊂ Int(X') is compact and ∂D is an analytic curve in X'. Here 'analytic' is for the natural real-analytic structure that ∂D inherits as the boundary of the conformal disc D.

The functors:
- (b) → (a): X = X' \ Int(D) and C = ∂D. Choosing the centre a reduces the real-projective structure of ∂D (structure group PGL(2,R) = GL(2,R)/R*) to the maximal compact subgroup O(2)/±1. This makes C an SO(2)-torsor.
- (a) → (b): glue the standard disc to C along the analytic parametrisation, which is well defined up to rotation (the 'bouchage des trous'). The conformal structure extends across C because the gluing is analytic (reflection principle). The point a is the centre of the glued disc.

In modern terms this is the equivalence between Riemann surfaces with an analytically parametrised boundary circle, here only up to rotation, and surfaces with a puncture plus a centred analytic disc around it. That is exactly the sewing data of Segal's axioms for conformal field theory and the geometric side of vertex algebras (Vafa; Huang).

Second paragraph: fix (X', a). The tangent plane T_{X',a} carries a canonical conformal (similarity) structure, so the round discs centred at 0 form an R*+-torsor, a 1-dimensional manifold.
- A disc D around a has a uniformisation φ: D → unit disc with φ(a) = 0, unique up to rotation.
- The composite (dφ_a)^{-1} ∘ φ: D → T_a is therefore canonical; this is the 'inclusion canonique D ⊂ T_{X',a}' of the previous page.
- Its image o(D), the 'ombre' (shadow) named on the next page, is the round disc whose radius is the conformal radius of D at a.

The next page notes three properties:
- D ↦ o(D) is monotone; this follows from the Schwarz lemma.
- It is not injective.
- It is equivariant for 'concentric' shrinking by λ ∈ ]0,1].

It then turns to compact X' with marked points a_i and disjoint discs D_i. It asks which further conditions on the distribution of the D_i would make the configuration determined by its shadows. This is in effect the classical extremal problem for conformal radii of non-overlapping domains, solved by Jenkins–Strebel quadratic differentials (the same data that give the ribbon-graph cell decomposition of M_{g,n}).

The purpose is to set up a cut-and-paste formalism for the moduli of marked conformal surfaces ('Chirurgie des surfaces conformes'), contemporaneous with the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: 'Rectifiable' is ambiguous. For the equivalence one needs ∂D, resp. C, to be real-analytic. With merely rectifiable or C^∞ boundary, conformal welding of the disc need not exist or be unique, so the extension of the conformal structure is not automatic. Grothendieck's own '(?)' signals the doubt.
The morphisms of the categories are not specified. Presumably isomorphisms are meant (groupoids), or open embeddings compatible with the data; the equivalence is only clear for isomorphisms.

In (a) no real-projective structure on C is given a priori. The torsor structure alone (an analytic parametrisation up to rotation) suffices, and the projective structure is then induced by the glued disc. The phrase 'compatible avec la structure de droite projective réelle' on the previous page only makes sense on the (b) side.
The 'inclusion canonique D ⊂ T_{X',a}' is canonical as a map, but its image is only the shadow o(D). D itself is not a subset of T_a; it is identified with o(D) via the normalised uniformisation.

ideas.what: Equivalence between surfaces with an analytically parametrised (up to rotation) boundary circle and surfaces with a centred analytic disc around a point; capping holes by gluing a disc
ideas.modern_name: Segal's sewing / Riemann surfaces with parametrised boundary vs punctures with local coordinates (moduli of bordered surfaces vs P(n) of Vafa–Huang)
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Segal (CFT definition, c. 1987), C. Vafa (1987), Y.-Z. Huang (1990s); classical gluing via reflection principle
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses cutting surfaces and the Teichmüller tower, but I do not recall this precise equivalence there

ideas.what: A centre in a disc is equivalent to reducing the real-projective structure of its boundary from PGL(2,R) to O(2)/±1, giving an SO(2)-torsor structure on the boundary circle
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of a point of the hyperbolic disc is a maximal compact SO(2) ⊂ PSL(2,R)

ideas.what: Shadow o(D) ⊂ T_{X',a}: canonical round disc in the tangent plane attached to a disc D around a, with monotonicity and homothety compatibility
ideas.modern_name: Conformal radius (inner radius / capacity data) of D at a, viewed as a norm or point of the R*+-torsor of round discs in T_a

ideas.what: Disjoint discs D_i around marked points a_i, and whether the configuration is determined by its shadows under further restrictive conditions
ideas.modern_name: Extremal problems for products of conformal radii of non-overlapping domains; Jenkins–Strebel quadratic differentials and ribbon-graph decompositions of M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lavrentiev, Goluzin, Jenkins, Kuz'mina, Strebel; Harer–Mumford–Thurston, Penner, Kontsevich for the moduli application

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck formulated the dictionary between bordered Riemann surfaces with boundary circles parametrised up to rotation and surfaces with marked points plus centred analytic discs. This is the basic sewing datum of Segal's later (1987) CFT axioms. Here it serves a programme of 'surgery' on the modular tower of the Esquisse, predating and independent of the physics-motivated literature.
missed.quote: Cat. des surfaces conformes à bord, compactes avec comp. connexe choisie C du bord, et une structure torsoriale disons rectifiable (?) ... Cat. des surfaces conformes X', avec disque pointé (D,a)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/historical point linking the Esquisse modular-tower programme to the operadic sewing structures (Segal, Huang, framed little discs, genus-zero operads acting on the Teichmüller tower) that later realised parts of it.

missed.claim: Through the 'ombres' (conformal radii as canonical round discs in the tangent spaces at the marked points), Grothendieck points toward attaching to marked surfaces with disjoint discs a configuration determined by tangent data. Under extremality this is the Jenkins–Strebel picture underlying the ribbon-graph/dessin description of moduli. The tangent-space formulation fits his tangential base points.
missed.quote: on prend une famille mutuellement disjointe D_i ... donnant des ombres o(D_i) ⊂ T_{X';a_i}. Une demande des conditions restrictives plus fines ... qu'il est déterminé par ... des ombres
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a possible precursor link, in Grothendieck's own words, between his dessins/tangential base point programme and the Strebel-differential cell decomposition (Harer, Penner, Kontsevich), later connected to dessins by Mulase–Penkava and others. It is largely an unfinished thread here.

deep.surprise_reason: The material itself is classical complex analysis: gluing discs and conformal radius. What is notable is the date and framing: a categorical sewing equivalence (bordered surfaces with boundary torsor vs pointed discs) and shadow data in tangent spaces, written c. 1983–84, before Segal's CFT formalism, as part of the Esquisse surgery programme. It is not a new theorem, so the surprise is moderate.
